about.title: Common sight words, set one
about.length_note: About 10 minutes fits six small words, a few short lines to read, and some letter choosing. You can pause after any step and come back, so take longer if you want.

say.text: Hello {name}. Today we meet six small words. You will see them again and again, so they are worth knowing at a glance.

show.text: Words you know at a glance

say.text: A sight word is a word you learn to know straight away, the way you know a friend's face. You do not need to sound it out each time. Some of these words do not sound the way they look, so knowing them by sight helps.

show.text: Sight word = a word you know at a glance

say.text: Here are today's six words. We will take them two at a time. Go slowly. There is no rush.

show.text: the  ·  a  ·  I  ·  to  ·  and  ·  is

say.text: First pair: the, and a. 'The' has three letters: t, h, e. 'A' is just one letter, and it is also a whole word. Say them out loud: the. A.
Second pair: I, and to. 'I' is one tall letter that is also a whole word. It is how we write about ourselves. 'To' has two letters: t, o. It sounds like 'too'. Say them: I. To.
Last pair: and, and is. 'And' joins things together, like 'tea and toast'. 'Is' says what something is, like 'the sun is hot'. Say them: and. Is.
Let's try one. Look at the short line and find the word 'is'.
say.note: Read the line out loud first.

ask.q: Which word in 'The dog is up.' is the word 'is'?
ask.why: 'Is' has two letters, i and s. It is the third word in the line.

say.text: Now a longer line. Many of our six words are hiding in it. Take your time and see how many you can spot: I, to, the, and, a, is.

show.text: I go to the shop and I see a bus.

ask.q: Which word in the line joins 'go to the shop' with 'I see a bus'?
ask.why: 'And' joins the two halves of the line together.

say.text: Now we spell by choosing letters. There is no typing. Just pick the right ones, in order. Let's spell 'to'. First t, then o.

ask.why: 'To' starts with t and ends with o. The sound is 'too', but the spelling is t, o.

say.text: One more. Spell 'and'. It starts with a, then n, then d.

ask.why: 'And' is a, then n, then d. Say it slowly and listen for each letter.

say.text: Well done, {name}. You met six words today: the, a, I, to, and, is. You will see them everywhere now. Next class we meet a second set. Rest if you need to, and come back whenever you like.

show.text: the · a · I · to · and · is
